findings.claim: The change deliberately generates a formatter in the consuming assembly for a type from a referenced assembly, which contradicts the earlier convention that referenced-assembly types get no formatter. The new behaviour is explicitly opt-in via [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] and is what REQ-2129 asks for, so L11 is not violated: TypeCollector's metadata early-return is untouched and no automatic generation occurs.

receipt_plan.detail: [L11] TypeCollector.CollectCore still returns early for metadata-only types (TypeCollector.cs:367-370); formatters for external types are produced only through the explicit opt-in GeneratedFormatterCollector path, so no defect.

findings.claim: The new public attribute GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute is added to MessagePack.Annotations without any PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt update visible in the diff, if the project tracks public API.

receipt_plan.detail: Check whether src/MessagePack.Annotations has PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt, and whether it lists GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute and SurrogateType. The diff contains no such update.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: The change implements the formatter-class attribute with contractless default plus an optional SurrogateType property (the maintainer's suggested design). Keys come from the surrogate's [Key] and [IgnoreMember] attributes, matched by member name. Only parameterless constructors and public read-write members are supported.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Support only the minimal contractless mode, with no SurrogateType. Honour attributes already on T (DataContract, DataMember, MessagePackObject, Key) and use no surrogate. This requires removing the SurrogateType property, the surrogate collector path and MsgPack022, and adding handling for attributes present on T.
